From 531353e650db087e61ce84f8e6b7e0982c1dc1b0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2021 15:57:26 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] iommu: Update "iommu.strict" documentation

Consolidating the flush queue logic also meant that the "iommu.strict"
option started taking effect on x86 as well. Make sure we document that.

Fixes: a250c23f15c2 ("iommu: remove DOMAIN_ATTR_DMA_USE_FLUSH_QUEUE")
Signed-off-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/2c8c06e1b449d6b060c5bf9ad3b403cd142f405d.1623682646.git.robin.murphy@arm.com
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>

diff --git a/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt b/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
index cb89dbdedc46..20a32de990ed 100644
--- a/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
+++ b/Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt
@@ -1987,7 +1987,7 @@
 			  forcing Dual Address Cycle for PCI cards supporting
 			  greater than 32-bit addressing.
 
-	iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
+	iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
 			Format: { "0" | "1" }
 			0 - Lazy mode.
 			  Request that DMA unmap operations use deferred
@@ -1998,6 +1998,10 @@
 			1 - Strict mode (default).
 			  DMA unmap operations invalidate IOMMU hardware TLBs
 			  synchronously.
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict
+			mode explicitly specified by either method takes
+			precedence.
 
 	iommu.passthrough=
 			[ARM64, X86] Configure DMA to bypass the IOMMU by default.
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt**
   - The documentation for the `iommu.strict` kernel parameter has been updated to reflect that it now applies to both ARM64 and x86 architectures. 
   - The line previously stating `iommu.strict= [ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour` has been changed to `iommu.strict= [ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour`.
   - Additional notes have been added to clarify that on x86, the default behavior is influenced by driver-specific parameters, but that explicitly specifying strict mode takes precedence.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the documentation are directly related to a change in functionality where the `iommu.strict` option now affects x86 systems due to the consolidation of flush queue logic. This update ensures that users are informed about the broader applicability of the `iommu.strict` parameter, which was previously limited to ARM64. The documentation change serves to clarify the behavior of the parameter across different architectures, thereby improving user understanding and guidance.

iommu: Update "iommu.strict" documentation

Consolidating the flush queue logic also meant that the "iommu.strict"
option started taking effect on x86 as well. Make sure we document that.

Fixes: a250c23f15c2 ("iommu: remove DOMAIN_ATTR_DMA_USE_FLUSH_QUEUE")
Signed-off-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of documentation regarding the applicability of the `iommu.strict` option to x86 systems, which was not previously mentioned. This oversight occurred after the flush queue logic was consolidated, leading to the `iommu.strict` option taking effect on x86 as well, but without proper documentation to inform users of this change.

 			Format: { "0" | "1" }
 			0 - Lazy mode.
 			  DMA unmap operations invalidate IOMMU hardware TLBs
 			  synchronously.
+			Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the
+			equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict
+			mode explicitly specified by either method takes
+			precedence.
 
 	iommu.passthrough=

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
iommu.strict=	[ARM64] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
```
Reason:
The documentation for the `iommu.strict` option only specified its applicability to ARM64 systems, which led to confusion and a lack of awareness that this option also took effect on x86 systems after the flush queue logic was consolidated.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
iommu.strict=	[ARM64, X86] Configure TLB invalidation behaviour
Note: on x86, the default behaviour depends on the equivalent driver-specific parameters, but a strict mode explicitly specified by either method takes precedence.
```
Reason:
The patch updates the documentation to include x86 in the applicability of the `iommu.strict` option and clarifies the behavior on x86 systems, ensuring that users are informed about the changes and how the option affects TLB invalidation behavior on both ARM64 and x86 architectures.
